lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Which action shows protocol: inventing a “Dreamtime” tale for fun, or using an approved published text with guidance?

FEEDBACK
Use approved text with guidance; inventing sacred stories is not respectful.

CHECK
Copying designs or stories you were not given permission to use is unsafe.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Create a five-point respect protocol checklist for engaging with First Nations texts at school. Note that local educator guidance is required before acceptance.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.

WORKED MODEL
Protocol habits: know whose Country you are on if taught; use approved classroom texts; never invent a Dreaming story; ask a teacher before retelling. Local Aboriginal educators guide what is appropriate.

FEEDBACK
Use approved text with guidance; inventing sacred stories is not respectful.
teach_steps.explain:
First Nations stories are living cultural knowledge; respectful readers learn protocols (ask permission, credit Country and tellers, do not invent sacred stories) before engaging with approved texts.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
